keyNotes: Mod 0302 vs both (2026-10-14): the density round's frontage brake held 235 of 279 checks (why=free): the mod built 122 demand edges in 20 builds against 1032 in 170 in 0119 (11 % of the edges against 24 %; the head start the same, 166 vs 151). The game grew the towns: exactly vanilla's people (41,963), vanilla's density (pb 6.33 vs 6.37, street 3.99 vs 3.78 m per person), but round and alike (spread 1.13 against 1.19 / 1.20, one town over 1.3 against four) and denser in the centre (63.5 persons / ha against 29.4).

Mod 0302: 3 satellites, 0 districts, 0 Works (0119: 8 / 9 / 3): their decisions only came with the 20 demand builds, and the 300-building gates were slow for vanilla-dense towns. Level weights on all 16 towns early, but no level 3-4 building anywhere: those exist only from 1950 / 1990 (findings towns.md).

Next build (NEXT_PHASE_BRIEF 40): no brake for young towns (under 1800 persons), brake and level weights phased in to 3600, offshoot turns and offshoot size in persons. Add its run with build_compare.py --add.

0119, mod vs vanilla: Buildings 15665 vs 6547 (x2.39) = persons x1.16 (48820 vs 42429 built capacity) times persons-per-building x2.06 (3.12 vs 6.48). Both runs reached 98-99 % of their SIMGROW target; vanilla kept up at every fill year (95-99 %), the mod lagged more (87-98 %).

0119, mod vs vanilla: By design (ot_driver FILL_EXTRA 0.15 per dose, FILL_CAP 1.3x base) the mod's dose fill leaves a town's initialLandUseCapacities higher: 7 towns ended x1.14-1.30 (Windermere 661->824, Darley Dale 484->627, Telscombe 485->631, Ringwood x1.15, Ellesmere Port x1.14, Blackwater x1.16, Whitehill x1.15), sum 6529 -> 7222 (+10.6 %). The growth target is initial x factor, and in SIMGROW experience grows with size, so the mod run's targets ended 16 % higher (49994 vs 42969).
0119, mod vs vanilla: The mod run also has 10 extra towns (7 districts, 3 Works; 669 buildings) not counted in SIMGROW or the 16-town metrics.
